lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
The input is 4 slices and each slice becomes one piece of toast. What is the output count, and which number was the input?

FEEDBACK
The input is 4 slices and the output is 4 pieces of toast, because each slice is toasted once and none are dropped. The check is 4 in equals 4 out. The toaster is still the tool, not the output. An output of 3 would mean one slice was never toasted, which this algorithm does not do.

WATCH FOR
A common mistake is to call the toaster the output, instead of counting the pieces of toast the algorithm produces. A tool does the work. The output is the result count.

WORKED MODEL
When the input is 2 slices and each slice is toasted once, the output is 2 pieces of toast, so 2 in equals 2 out. The input is chosen before the steps run. The output is the count you can check at the end. If the algorithm dropped a slice, the output would be 1, and 2 in would not equal 1 out. That drop is not part of this algorithm, so the honest output is 2.
